narrative.overview:
The Sketch design system treats the digital surface as a living desk workspace—a shared working sheet composed of tactile warm paper, dark pencil ink, blue marginalia, red editorial revisions, and soft yellow highlights. It balances the immediate human intimacy of hand-drafted notes with rigorous underlying typography and structured information hierarchy.

Rather than sterile digital perfection or noisy skeuomorphism, Sketch uses intentional paper scraps, fine 1.5px pencil strokes, and slight organic rotations (-1° to 1.5°) to create a thoughtful craft aesthetic. Whitespace functions as open thought space, ensuring uninterrupted reading flow, instant scanability, and clear calls to action.
keyCharacteristics: Warm Living Paper: Unbleached warm ground (#f7f2e7) with graphite ink (#38352f) and lighter scraps (#fcf8ef).
Original Handwritten Pairing: Bold Working Marker paired with comfortable, spacious Working Hand.
Annotative Color Roles: Blue notes, red corrections, and pale yellow highlights.
Organic Affordance: Uneven hand-drawn borders, tactile hard offsets, and taped editorial references.
Accessible Foundations: Semantic HTML controls, dashed blue focus indicators, and reduced-motion support.

rules.name: The Paper & Pencil Rule
rules.body: White #FFFFFF is never used as an open canvas; all surfaces start on warm paper ground (#f7f2e7), and text uses graphite ink (#38352f) to maintain warm paper coherence.

rules.name: The Red Correction Rule
rules.body: Red (#9e3a2e) is reserved for singular high-leverage actions and corrections. It appears on no more than 10% of any given view to maintain its urgency.

rules.name: The Intentional Scrap Rule
rules.body: Lighter paper scraps (#fcf8ef) must never be stacked haphazardly; each scrap corresponds to a discrete thought, quote, or taped reference.

rules.name: The Breathing Room Rule
rules.body: Handwritten text runs together if tightly tracked or set in narrow line heights. Body handwriting must maintain line-height: 1.5 and at least 23px base size.

rules.name: The Selective Tilt Rule
rules.body: Rotations are applied only to discrete notes, tape strips, or occasional standalone headings (-1° to 1.5°). Continuous paragraphs remain untransformed to preserve effortless reading.

rules.name: The Zero-Blur Rule
rules.body: Soft Gaussian shadows are strictly prohibited. Depth is rendered solely through crisp 1-2px hard offsets and physical tonal contrast.

rules.name: The Paper Settle Rule
rules.body: Active/pressed controls physically compress down onto the sheet, collapsing their offset shadow to 0px.

rules.name: The Organic Edge Rule
rules.body: Buttons and containers must use asymmetric border-radius shorthand to avoid cold, machine-cut rectangular boxes.

rules.name: The Restrained Texture Rule
rules.body: No heavy crumpled paper noise or distracting SVG turbulence. Clean, subtle grain or untextured flat warm sheets preserve legibility.

dos: Do maintain authentic semantic controls (<button>, <a>, <details>, <input>) beneath all sketch styling.
Do keep reading handwriting generously sized (minimum 23px for reading, 24px for body) to ensure continuous legibility.
Do use a visible 2px dashed blue (#344c69) focus outline for all interactive elements to guarantee keyboard accessibility.
Do preserve actual photograph detail inside pale paper mounts rather than post-processing pictures into fake drawings.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion by removing tilts and transforms while preserving state color and stroke feedback.
Do use generous spacing between open thought sections to keep the working sheet uncluttered and comfortable to read.
donts: Don't use illegible, ornate cursive or script fonts that make words difficult to decipher.
Don't apply heavy crumpled-paper textures, noisy skeuomorphic overlays, or dense doodle borders that distract from content.
Don't use soft Gaussian drop shadows or polished geometric cards.
Don't animate strokes drawing themselves across the page; keep drawings, handwriting, and paper still.
Don't tilt entire paragraphs or large content blocks; limit small rotations to buttons, tape strips, and scrap notes.
Don't obscure text or alter natural document reading order with decorative annotations.
